# Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate
> each answer token (decode), although generation is almost all decoding. With LoopBridge, a small adapter (LoRA + per-loop
> key-value maps on a frozen model), a decoder with n loops reads the prompt states of any prefill depth m. The paper
> measures where inference time goes, how accuracy changes with m = 1..16 at fixed n, and how more prefill loops compare
> at equal measured time with the original model, distilled models and more decode loops (Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking,
> Ouro-1.4B). Every number is recomputed from released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (Ouro-2.6B; 95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- Prefill is 0.1-3% of the time of a chain-of-thought answer.
- Same weights, one decode loop: four prefill loops instead of one raise the 11-benchmark average from 47.2 to 56.8
  (gain 9.0 +- 0.6 over three seeds); on most benchmarks the gain stops at two to four prefill loops.
- Equal measured time: Ours 4/1 is 14.2 points above Original 1/1 and 7.0 above Distilled 1/1 at about the same time;
  a second decode loop buys 15.5 points for 1.4x the time; at two decode loops more prefill loops and distillation tie.
- Baselines: the distilled controls move by at most 0.6 points over 0.3x-3x learning rates and at rank 80.
- Exceptions: 4-shot MATH-500 (prefill 1 best; 0-shot reverses it) and HELMET exact recall.

Limitations stated by the author: timing at batch 1 on one GPU type; the prefill depth is chosen per benchmark, not
routed per prompt; the prefill loops stay frozen; models are 1.4B-2.6B with four native loops; English benchmarks.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands
- paper/untying-prefill-decode-loops.pdf: the paper
- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: the recomputed statistics
- ouro/results/provenance/: command, configuration, checkpoint hash, log and outputs of every run
